args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api deployment v2.3.1 (seq 3, production) began failing health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of 18%. v2.3.1 is recorded as unhealthy in the release history.

Remediation: Rolled back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release previously healthy in production (no change-manager approval required, as v2.3.0 has a prior healthy production record). The first rollback attempt halted after us-east due to an orchestrator error, leaving the service in a mixed state (us-east=v2.3.0, us-west/eu-west=v2.3.1). A retry completed the rollout. All three regions are now on v2.3.0 and the service reports healthy with error rate down to ~0.2%.

Note: v2.3.1-rc is marked unhealthy in staging, suggesting the defect was present pre-release. Recommended follow-ups: root-cause the v2.3.1 regression and verify the staging health gating before any re-deploy of v2.3.1.

trace.final:
Done. The timeout was only in the response path — the incident was created successfully as INC-0001.

## Summary

**Diagnosis:** checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate. Release history confirmed v2.3.1 as `unhealthy` in production.

**Target version:** v2.3.0 — the most recent release with a healthy production record. I skipped v2.3.1-rc since it's a staging-only build and itself marked unhealthy. Per policy, no change-manager approval was needed because v2.3.0 has previously been healthy in production.

**Rollback:** The first attempt halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving a genuinely risky split state (us-east=v2.3.0, us-west/eu-west=v2.3.1). I verified the partial state rather than assuming success, then retried, which completed cleanly across all regions.

**Result:** All regions on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate 18% → 0.2%.

**Incident:** SEV2 opened as INC-0001, documenting the failure, the partial-rollback-and-retry sequence, and the current healthy state.

**Recommendations for follow-up:**
- Root-cause the v2.3.1 regression before any re-deploy.
- The unhealthy `v2.3.1-rc` in staging suggests the defect was visible pre-release — worth reviewing why staging health gating didn't block the production promotion.

One caveat worth flagging: because the first rollback partially applied, checkout-api was serving two different versions simultaneously for that window. If you see anomalies in checkout data from that period, that's the likely cause.
